answer: Reputation-Weighted Escrow Decay. Each new identity must escrow a starting balance that decays toward zero unless it earns verified counterparty ratings; the curve steepens with cluster density, so linked identities pay escalating escrow. An attacker's per-identity cost rises like a crystal lattice as the cluster grows, not a fixed fee. Clean actors recover escrow like polished marble over time. A cedar threshold of ratings releases funds; below it, escrow is forfeited. Sybils thus face superlinear capital lockup per fake identity.
